Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has caused widespread illness and death, with cell death from pyroptosis being a key contributor to its pathogenicity. Pyroptosis is a form of programmed cell death characterized by the rupture of infected cells, releasing cytokines that exacerbate the viral load. Understanding the temporal cell death cycle and the underlying pathway is essential to developing effective strategies to combat the pandemic. This project applies a differential equation-based single-cell model to simulate the NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis pathway in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells, with the aim of analyzing the impact of anti-inflammatory treatments on the cell death cycle. By fitting the model to experimental data, we obtained a comprehensive understanding of how the caspase-1 and gasdermin-B (GSDM) pathways intersect, with caspase-1 being the primary executor of cell death. Furthermore, our analysis indicates that inhibiting NLRP3 or caspase-1 could delay cell death, while GSDM, being an alternative pathway, may offer cross-talk-mediated protection against pyroptotic cell death. This model can be utilized to explore various anti-inflammatory treatment strategies and their effects on the pyroptosis pathway. Additionally, we have made the model publicly available for the scientific community to further investigate how it can be applied to tackling the pandemic. Leveraging this model, our analysis recommends the development of caspase-1 inhibitors as a potential therapeutic approach to mitigating the spread of the virus. This suggestion is backed by the fact that delaying cell death through such inhibition could allow the immune system sufficient time to eliminate the infected cells. This concept has been graphically represented through an interactive dashboard available on SHINY. This model and its outcomes highlight the value of mathematical modeling in identifying the critical roles that caspase-1 and gasdermin-B play in the pyroptosis pathway and the potential of modeling to inform the development of novel therapeutic approaches against SARS-CoV-2. Furthermore, it underscores the significance of collaborative research between mathematical modeling and experimental biology in the pursuit of understanding the pandemic and developing effective treatments. This research was a collaborative effort between the University of Surrey and the University of Hertfordshire. It has been funded by the University of Surrey through the Covid-19 research grant. This inaccuracy results because the sampling process introduces inaccurate phase information due to uncorrelated signals from neighboring elements, causing a synthetic aperture to incorrectly position soft tissue. To resolve this issue, we introduce a novel technique, where the sampling process is reinterpreted as a form of coherent integration. By applying the virtual source synthetic aperture method, we first separate the phase information into system and sample components. We then use the sample-specific phase to calculate the lateral shift, followed by the synthesis of images using this accurate estimation. Our results show that the virtual source synthetic aperture method yields images with a 65% lower mean squared error compared to conventional synthetic aperture, and the axially extended synthetic aperture variant achieves a 25% lower mean squared error. Imperative algorithms and logical proofs in sequent calculus or natural deduction coexist as distinct yet related concepts. This integration of computer science and logical knowledge can be further expanded by incorporating additional fundamental theories, such as sets, numbers, and stability properties. To illustrate this integration, we reframe the natural deduction rules for basic propositional and predicate logic as pseudocodes, offering a more expressive language that combines the expressive power of natural deductions with the executability of pseudocodes. This hybrid language allows us to define fundamental notions like computability, decidability, and the relationship between logical validity and computability. Building on this foundation, we investigate the properties of this hybrid language, considering examples of fundamental theories that can be expressed within it. Furthermore, we outline a straightforward extension to enable the specification of stability properties for recursive functions. This extended framework enables us to explore more intricate topics, such as the computability of the halting problem and the limitations of natural deduction with recursive functions. By defining the rules for converting natural deductions into pseudocodes and vice versa, we can translate any natural deduction with recursive functions into an equivalent algorithm and conversely, any execution of this algorithm into a corresponding natural deduction. This correspondence holds the key to understanding how the executability of pseudocodes reflects the soundness of the associated natural deductions. This connection allows us to prove the correctness of programs by demonstrating the derivability of their specifications from given assumptions. This way, we can integrate the expressive power of natural deductions with the executability of pseudocodes, offering a more comprehensive and coherent programming paradigm that combines the strengths of both approaches. This extended abstract is based on prior research and presents an initial outline of the topics to be explored in the accompanying presentation. This presentation will provide a more detailed examination of the issues, accompanied by concrete examples and an overview of the current state of the art in this area. This includes an examination of the relationship between natural deductions and pseudocodes, the decision-making capabilities of algorithms, the computability of the halting problem, the limitations of natural deductions with recursive functions, and the connections between natural deductions, pseudocodes, and the stability properties of recursive functions. To study the rotational characteristics of exotic, distorted halo nuclei like
$^{48}$Mg, researchers employed the angular momentum projection method onto
single-particle wave functions within the mean-field framework. This approach
involved the use of the deformed Hartree-Fock method. By analyzing the intrinsic
configurations of these nuclei via the symmetry properties of the angular
momentum projection, a detailed understanding of the rotational structure was
gained. It was found that in $^{48}$Mg, the 0h$\oplus$4h rotational band has a
prolate deformed shape, distinct from the intrinsic shape of the 2h$\oplus$4h
rotational band, which is characterized by an oblate-deformed or halo shape.
Consequently, the excitation energies of the 2h$\oplus$4h band are elevated due to
the coupling of the 2h rotational motion with the 4h motion, resulting in an
oblate-deformed or halo shape. Similarly, in $^{50}$Mg, the 0h$\oplus$5h
rotational band exhibits a prolate-deformed shape, whereas the 2h$\oplus$5h
rotational band is predicted to have an elevated excitation energy and an
oblate-deformed or halo shape. This predicts the occurrence of shape
decoupling effects in $^{49,50}$Mg. Moreover, the calculated electric dipole
transition probabilities from the 2h$\oplus$4h or 2h$\oplus$5h rotational bands
to the 0h$\oplus$4h or 0h$\oplus$5h rotational band are anticipated to be
experimentally observable with current detection capabilities. Hence, a study
of these nuclei using an (e, e'$\gamma$) reaction or other experimental methods
is highly recommended. A comparison with existing experimental data and a
prediction of new observables in $^{48,50}$Mg are presented in this study. Le

This paper presents the effective vector boson approximation (eva) method for describing the interactions of weak bosons in a context where their masses can be safely neglected, a scenario applicable to the conditions found in muon colliders.
The eva framework is comprehensive, addressing all possible combinations of weak bosons, their associated virtual loops, and the relevant subprocesses, and is highly efficient, with a computational cost significantly lower than full-event simulations.
To verify the eva method's accuracy, this paper compares eva predictions to corresponding results from full shower simulations for a variety of scenarios, including top quark production, gauge boson scattering, and vector boson fusion processes, and shows that the method's assumptions hold true for energies above 0.75 TeV and integrated luminosities exceeding 0.5 inverse femtometers squared. As such, the eva method becomes a useful tool for accurately modeling muon collider environments and effectively incorporating experimental data into phenomenological analyses. Furthermore, this approach facilitates the strategic selection of relevant irreducible signatures for signature-based analyses, thereby significantly reducing computational costs and making such studies at muon colliders feasible. We examine how the incompleteness theorems of Godel, combined with the eventual discovery of the consistency theorem by Godel, influenced the work of logicians Tarski, Carnap, and Rosser. Our research reveals the complex interplay between these logicians in the 1930s-1950s, a period marked by both collaboration and competition. Despite facing significant obstacles, including Godel's secretive publication practices and language barriers, ouropic Godel, Tarski, Carnap, and Rosser managed to establish a spirit of mutual respect and a shared passion for advancing the field of mathematical logic. At the heart of our analysis lies an in-depth look at the epistolary exchange between Godel and Tarski, a pivotal aspect of the historical record that has only become fully accessible in recent years. Through a detailed review of the known facts and a new examination of a previously unreported conversation between Godel and Tarski, we gain a more comprehensive understanding of the relationships between these logical giants. Furthermore, we explore how the work of Godel, Tarski, Carnap, and Rosser continues to shape the field of mathematical logic to this very day. By exploring the personal lives and professional achievements of these logicians, we uncover a rich tapestry of cross-cultural collaboration, a unique aspect of the intellectual history of the 20th century. At the same time, our research highlights the significant role that three refugees from Nazi-occupied Europe, Godel, Tarski, and Carnap, played in shaping the field of mathematical logic in the United States. Additionally, we examine how the work of these logicians was influenced by the political upheaval of their time and the personal sacrifices they made in the name of their craft. By exploring the gathering of Godel, Tarski, Carnap, and Rosser in Los Angeles in 1936-1937, we gain a more comprehensive understanding of the relationships between these logical giants and the significant contributions they made to the advancement of mathematical logic. Furthermore, we uncover a previously unreported conversation between Godel and Tarski that reveals the complexities of their epistolary exchange and the difficulties they faced as logicians working across language and cultural barriers. This paper confirms the Three Balls Conjecture for functions satisfying certain properties, specifically those related to the Helmholtz equation and its eigenfunctions, within a specific mathematical framework. We examine the given equation in a computational framework and derive conditions under which it applies. Subsequent analysis on the eigenfunctions leads to an inequality that supports the Three Balls Conjecture. We also establish a link between this conjecture and another mathematical hypothesis. Through a transformation, we confirm the Three Balls Conjecture for functions subject to specific constraints, thereby providing a general solution. This solution is then applied to the eigenfunctions of the given equation, thus confirming the Three Balls Conjecture in a broader context. The proof of the conjecture is a direct outcome of our analysis on the eigenfunctions and their associated properties. Finally, we discuss an alternative approach to proving the conjecture and highlight the novel aspects of our proof, particularly in relation to the monic condition. This condition enables us to establish a more direct link between the algebraic and geometric components of the eigenfunctions and their respective moments. This connection becomes a fundamental aspect in our proof of the Three Balls Conjecture. The knowledge gained from this proof can be utilized in a broader context, encompassing not just the eigenfunctions of the Helmholtz equation but a more expansive class of functions defined by the Malmquist-Takenaka operator. This operator, at the heart of the Clifford analysis, encompasses the Helmholtz equation as a specific case, thereby enabling the extension of our proof to this broader class of functions. The name "Clifford Analysis" for this theoretical framework was chosen to distinguish it from the traditional approach based on vector techniques and instead emphasize its roots in the extensive algebra developed by Clifford in the 19th century. This historical context, coupled with the unique properties of the Clifford algebras, gives the functions within this analytical framework a distinct characteristic - namely that any monogenic function in n-dimensional space can be expressed as a sum of n linear terms. This fundamental property provides the underlying reason for the applicability of the Four Balls Theorem, as demonstrated by the renowned mathematician and one of the founders of the Overdetermined PDEs school, Professor Alan Koch. Furthermore, our analysis on the eigenfunctions of the Helmholtz equation can be seen as an extension of this property to the linear combinations of the powers of the monogenic functions. In this extended context, our proof of the Three Balls Conjecture for these eigenfunctions serves as a validation

To automate the process of image acquisition in tasks involving 3D reconstruction, arranging an eye-in-hand camera is a crucial step. Conventional methods primarily rely on 3D information from multiple images or use specialized sensors. In contrast, our research focuses on leveraging two-dimensional information from a single image to train a model that can predict optimal camera positions for 3D points of interest. By incorporating context from surrounding pixels through spatial attention mechanisms and making predictions in a probabilistic manner, our model can effectively handle real-world images with diverse lighting conditions and capture the ambiguities inherent to camera calibration. Through the use of the NYUD-V2 dataset, our algorithm achieves a median error of 0.56 degrees when optimizing cross-enterprise 3D alignment and a median error of 0.21 when optimizing within the same enterprise, indicating a model's ability to generalize across various scenes. The code for our approach has been made publicly available on GitHub. Furthermore, through the application of our model in a vision-based grasping task, a success rate of 80% was attained on the NYUD-V2 test set, demonstrating its utility in real-world scenarios. In comparison to existing approaches, our method surpasses baselines in tasks involving 3D reconstruction and grasping, as evidenced by the experimental results presented in this report. In solving inverse problems, researchers strive to restore a degraded or incomplete image based on available data. This is crucial in imaging techniques such as MRI, computed tomography, deblurring and super-resolution, among others. Because there can be multiple plausible images given the measurements, the key challenge lies in modeling the set of possible outcomes - the Bayesian posterior distribution. Our goal is to use a regularized conditional GAN to estimate the density of this distribution. By incorporating regularization on the generator, we can obtain a theoretically optimal truncation of the posterior distribution. This is achieved through the minimization of a truncated Kullback-Leibler divergence, which guarantees the existence of a global minimum. We can then apply various regularization techniques such as gradient penalty, batch normalization and spectral normalization to ensure the generator's well-definedness. Our method surpasses conventional techniques like the minimum variance estimator in theoretical efficiency and is particularly effective in complex data sets, as demonstrated by our MRI reconstruction examples. Additionally, we show that our approach can produce biologically plausible images in an MRI fatty tissue segmentation example, in comparison to the conventional method. Our code is openly accessible on https://github.com/zheng-ec/CGAN-PRI. Moreover, with the inclusion of metadata into complex data sets, our method facilitates efficient posterior sampling, which is highlighted through an example of a segmentation task in an MRI volume. Interestingly, we find that our scheme can yield an inference to a Truncated Normal distribution when the prior and measurement model are linear and Gaussian, respectively. In such a scenario, the distribution's parameters can be determined through an inverse problem under additional constraints. Lastly, we utilize a numerical linear algebra approach to solve an MRI reconstruction problem that involves low-rank positive semi-definite matrices, a problem that is otherwise non-convex. Our proposed method exhibits results that are as effective as current state-of-the-art algorithms but with the advantage of being computationally more efficient and direct. Furthermore, our results are analytically characterized, which is a complex issue that has yet to be resolved with deep learning-based algorithms. Our results with a particular example suggest that our method can be an optimization-based interpretation of some deep learning-based algorithms that solve similar problems. In particular, we found that when the prior and measurement model are linear and Gaussian, respectively, our scheme can determine an approximation of a factorization of the covariance matrix of the posterior distribution. This article examines the existence of invariant surfaces in a specific class of dynamical systems characterized by non-local feedback controllers, which rely on fractional-order integrals with a memory alpha in their control law. By applying a transformation to the partial differential equation and subsequent stability analysis using the Lyapunov direct method, we derive a sufficient condition for the non-existence of invariant surfaces in a neighborhood of the origin. The condition is expressed in terms of the coefficients of the system and the memory parameter alpha, which indicates that an invariant surface cannot be found when alpha is less than one. This conclusion is validated through numerical examples and contrasted with the behavior of traditional hyperlocal feedback controllers. The implications of these findings for the application of fractional-order controllers are also considered. The approach employed in this article is equally applicable to systems featuring difference operators with a memory alpha. Next-generation wireless networks face significant challenges due to high frequency THz communications' limited coverage and strong signal attenuation. Our research focuses on multi-hop THz communications by combining LiDAR technology and beam training to optimize communication links. However, rapidly fluctuating line-of-sight conditions pose significant challenges, requiring continuous adaptation of communication links. We've developed a novel approach where the base station uses a limited number of training signals to identify the optimal communication link, and we've modeled this optimization problem using a partially observable Markov decision process. Our primary objective is to minimize the number of training signals needed to adapt to changing line-of-sight conditions, while our secondary objective is to maximize the achieved data rate. We've derived an optimal solution for a simplified scenario and developed a machine learning-based approach for more complex scenarios, applying deep reinforcement learning to find the optimal communication link. Our simulation results confirm that our proposed scheme significantly improves data rates in multiple scenario scenarios. This research provides a new framework for optimizing the performance of multi-hop THz communications links. Additionally, our results demonstrate the efficacy of deep reinforcement learning in solving complex communication optimization problems. Finally, our study highlights the value of integrating LiDAR technology with communication systems to create a new generation of adaptive communication protocols. Furthermore, our outcome illustrates the potential of multi-agent reinforcement learning in solving complex communication challenges. Lastly, our analysis reveals the potential to further improve the performance of THz communications by optimizing the design of communication protocols and antennas. This paves the way for exploring novel designs that adapt to changing line-of-sight conditions in real-time, leading to a significant improvement in data transfer rates. As such, our proposed scheme offers a groundbreaking achievement in the field of wireless communications, providing a superior level of performance, and setting a new benchmark for future research to strive for. Observations of pulsar scintillation in the GHz frequency range offer a unique view into the structure of the interstellar medium, specifically the small-scale plasma obstacles and the phase screen caused by dense ionized regions in the line of sight to the pulsar. Pulsars that are easily observable from almost any location on Earth are ideal for conducting a systematic study of the interstellar medium across different regions of the sky. Between 2011 and 2019, the GBT collected nearly 600 hours of data on the pulsar PSR B1133+16, which can be used in conjunction with previous Arecibo and Parkes data for a comprehensive analysis. By modeling the variation in angular sizes and shape of the scintillation pattern, researchers were able to estimate the impact of line-of-sight structure on 20 different transverse baselines, accounting for any unresolved components. Our observations show that the line-of-sight turbulence exhibits a scale-independent behavior consistent with a Kolmogorov spectrum, with a characteristic angular size of around 0.38 seconds of arc at a particular scale. This finding is comparable to previous results for the North Polar Spur and a region near the Cygnus X-1 X-ray binary, but stands in contrast to a region containing the Eagle nebula, where a different pulsar shows an abnormal 1.5 times larger scale of around 0.54 seconds of arc. Our research also provides a visual representation of the line-of-sight structure of the interstellar medium through a phase diagram, which reveals a dense ionized region approximately 300 parsecs from the Earth and extending towards the Sun. This unique perspective on the interstellar medium also reveals a large, less dense ionized region approximately 1000 parsecs from the Earth, which contains a 10^11 M_{\odot}~$10^{10}~M_{\odot}$ mass range of intermediate-mass stars at twice the Sun's distance. This study presents a generative model called Quasi-Periodic WaveNet (QPNet) to enhance the raw waveform generative capabilities of WaveNet through pitch-dependent expanded convolution neural networks. By integrating pitch-dependent extended layers into the WaveNet framework, QPNet effectively captures both short-term and long-term periodic signal patterns within audio signals. Utilizing a pitch extraction module derived from the MEL Spectrogram, the model leverages pitch information obtained from this intermediate representation to generate high-fidelity speech samples. Experimentation reveals that QPNet surpasses the performance of baseline models, including WaveNet, CNN-RNN, and Multi-Scale WaveNet, in terms of naturalness and perceptual quality as evaluated by subjective listening tests and the Objective Naturalness Assessment of Raw Waveforms (ONRW). Notably, the results show a significant 0.090 score point improvement in mean objective naturalness score (MOS) when compared to the best competing model. The model's effectiveness is also demonstrated through reduced mean absolute error (MAE) values when estimating the MOS from the ONRW. The implementation of pitch-dependent expanded layers in QPNet enables the efficient generation of high-quality speech samples from raw waveforms by processing quasi-periodic signals with variable duration patterns. The proposed architecture provides a versatile framework that can be applied across various signal generation applications involving the creation of raw waveform models from time-series data exhibiting quasi-periodic patterns. This research presents a novel online annotation tool called MADARi, which serves as a spelling correction platform for Standard Arabic texts. Unlike other systems, MADARi uniquely addresses both the spelling and morphological aspects of Arabic, allowing users to correct spelling errors while applying morphological annotations. This unique feature sets MADARi apart from conventional systems, which either focus solely on spelling correction or morphological annotation. Our system utilizes a unique combination of rule-based and statistical methods to validate the consistency of both spelling and morphological annotations. This consistency check involves verifying that the base form of each word is correctly formed and present in the appropriate state (nominate or accusative). Additionally, MADARi checks the consistency of the root letter pattern for each submitted word, comparing it to the predefined list available on the platform. This innovative approach makes MADARi an effective tool for correcting spelling errors and standardizing Arabic text, which could potentially be utilized as a collaborative platform allowing multiple annotators to work together. Our research also explores the potential of using this tool to create a large-scale corpus of annotated Arabic texts. This could be particularly useful for machine learning models, which often rely on such resources to develop their language understanding. To demonstrate the efficacy of MADARi, we conducted a study using a set of poorly spelled Arabic texts, correcting the spelling errors and standardizing the morphological annotations using our platform. The results show significant improvements in both spelling and morphological accuracy. This led us to create a large-scale dataset of 2000 annotated Arabic words, which we believe could be beneficial for future machine learning applications. This research was conducted under the supervision of Dr. Abdaoui and Dr. Rosso. The paper will be presented at the 13th International Conference on Natural Language and Applied Computing (CIAA 2022) in Geneva, Switzerland. The development of advanced detection algorithms through deep learning has accelerated the identification of road issues, including automatic marking of defects from images. However, the current methodologies lack a unified framework that can efficiently analyze multiple image types captured during normal driving conditions. To address this challenge, we present RoadAtlas, a comprehensive system that utilizes a deep learning-based detection algorithm to analyze in-vehicle camera images, allowing for the simultaneous identification and mapping of road flaws in real-time. Furthermore, the system leverages geographic information and user feedback to create a detailed database of road conditions and associated issues, including locations, types, and severity levels. This integrated approach enables data analysis and visualization tools to provide critical information for maintenance prioritization, enabling users to focus on areas that require immediate attention based on flaw severity, location, and type. Through the utilization of cloud-based services and modular software architecture, RoadAtlas provides a versatile solution that can be easily implemented and adapted in various settings. The system's capabilities and features are showcased through a case study involving the management of road flaws in the city of Oulu, Finland. The study demonstrates the benefits of using the system in maintaining urban roads, highlighting the importance of regular update cycles and accurate input from drivers. Let G be an abelian group and A a nonempty subset of G, with elements denoted as $a_0, a_1,...,a_{2^k-1}$. The restricted signed sumset of A, written as $k\hat{+}A$, consists of all elements obtained from the sums $a_I = \sum_{i\in I}a_i$, where I is a nonempty subset of the index set $\{0,1,...,2^k-1\}$. The purpose of this paper is to prove the general form of the Chuang-Chang conjecture, specifically for restricted signed sumsets, and to provide a counterexample for $k\ge3$ in the integers. Furthermore, a part of the paper involves finding all pairs $(k,\lambda)$ with $k\ge3$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb{Z}$, for which the inequality $\lambda|A|_\infty\le|k\hat{+}A|$ holds true. Additionally, this paper extends a previous result from Feige and Schechtman regarding the sumset A+\_A, and provides a counterexample for this type of sumset when $k\ge3$ in the integers. The connection between $k\hat{+}A$ and A+\_A is also established through a restriction of A+\_A, leading to a further result or counterexample in A+\_A implying the same in $k\hat{+}A$ and vice versa. Lastly, this paper concludes with a conjecture regarding the further restriction of A+\_A. The main techniques employed in this paper involve applying the nonretrivable pairs method and a result from the authors and Li, in addition to modifying and extending the previously mentioned results from Chang, Chang and Li, and from Li and Zhai. The findings from this paper can also be seen as a part of the wider research into the general form of the Chuang-Chang conjecture. Characterizing colorectal polyps histology involves determining the type of polyp and its level of abnormality. A reliable diagnostic system for this purpose would greatly assist clinicians in making informed decisions about treatment and further investigation. However, developing such a system is challenging due to the diverse range of colorectal polyps and the subjectivity of grading their level of abnormality, which is compounded by the difficulty of compiling large datasets of annotated histological images.

Our project involves assembling the UniToPatho dataset, which comprises 2000 annotated H&E stained colon polyp images divided into three categories based on their level of abnormality (mild, moderate, severe). These annotations serve as a reference point for evaluating the system's accuracy in assessing the level of abnormality. Furthermore, our research involves exploring multiple models for classifying and grading the level of abnormality and presents a comprehensive evaluation of their performance. 

For classification, our primary focus was on distinguishing between normal and abnormal samples. In contrast, for grading, we explored different approaches using deep learning architectures and established a point-system method leading to the development of a open-source, customizable framework called PoinTNet. This framework enables the creation of custom point systems for grading the level of abnormality and provides a flexible framework for users to implement their own post-processing techniques.

In our experiments, a baseline convolutional neural network was used as a starting point and different architectures such as multi-scale point networks and more complex models like UNet and EfficientNet were examined. We found that UNet produced the best results for both classification and grading, outperforming the state-of-the-art in a recent study cited in our research. Notably, our UniToPatho dataset surpasses all existing datasets in terms of size and has been made available for public access, enabling the advancement of computational methods for diagnosing colorectal polyps. Our research offers a versatile solution that can be utilized by both academic and industrial practitioners, and the underlying architecture of our model has been thoroughly explored through numerical experiments and a comprehensive analysis. Finally, our study is also accompanied by an user-friendly web application that enables users to easily explore and visualize the underlying histology images, providing a more comprehensive understanding of the Polyp field. This application is available at https://unito-pathology.granoofcode.com/. UniToPatho is the first comprehensive dataset for colorectal polyps, addressing the lack of standardized and widely-accepted classification systems currently employed in clinical settings. We analyzed the isotopic composition of hydrogen in pyroxene minerals from two chondrite meteorites, finding a higher deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio in pyroxene from the Chelyabinsk meteorite. This increase is attributed to a greater exchange of deuterium with water in the meteorite parent body during its final stages of development. The variation in deuterium-to-hydrogen ratios in pyroxene minerals from both meteorites suggests that the water in the inner solar system's planetesimals underwent partial exchange with the accretion nebula's nebular water, leaving a signature of the nebula's $\delta$D of -40 $\pm$ 20. This exchange occurred as the nebula's gas was slowly consumed by the growing body, and was more pronounced in smaller bodies like the Chelyabinsk-type asteroids. This finding provides new evidence for the nebula's water to have originated from multiple sources, with implications for the origin of Earth's water and the formation of super-Earths. Furthermore, it highlights the importance of considering the effects of nebular gas consumption in models of planetary accretion, and suggests that the inner solar system's small bodies should exhibit a range of water isotope compositions reflecting their formation under varying nebular conditions. Additionally, the observed variation in deuterium-to-hydrogen ratios in pyroxene minerals from both meteorites raises implications for the formation of multiple planetisimals from a single parent body, such as Mars, which could have a water isotope composition that is an average of that of its building blocks.

Speech translation combines speech recognition and machine translation to enable
language interpretation for those who cannot communicate effectively due to
language barriers. Advanced systems have achieved substantial progress in various
settings, including systems that can translate speech independently, remove
background noise, and handle multi-speaker environments. However, current systems
require the same medium for input and output - for example, speech to speech,
with no ability to convert speech to text and then text to speech in another
language. This project explores the idea of translating speech directly into a
different language, bypassing the intermediate text form, and acknowledges
the significant challenge this poses due to the high dimensional nature of speech
data. To tackle this, we propose new types of cross-domain alignments and a
comprehensive system that can learn to perform this complex task. Despite having
no training data for a particular language pair, our system is able to
demonstrate its capabilities on a previously untried Spanish to French speech
translation task, with a notable gap remaining between human and machine
performance. Notably, our system achieves this zero-shot translation capability
without the need for additional parameters in relation to multilingual speechto-speech translation models. Our findings validate the potential of this zero-shot speech translation approach, with potential future improvements to be
gained from a more extensive system evaluation and a more intricate model
architecture. Our code is available at https://github.com/parag-sitajit/zero-shot-speech-translation. Our model performance is presented at tab.1 of our paper and the audio samples for our evaluation are available at https://speechkitten.github.io/zero-shot-speech-translation/, with more detailed information available in our paper "Zero-shot Speech Translation" (arXiv 2206.15031). Unsurprisingly, the Mie solution delivers the most precise results, achieving a high degree of accuracy even when the particles are relatively close together. While the superposition method also yields reliable results for large distances and differences between the dimensions of particles, it can be less accurate when the particles are small or closely aligned. We introduce a new, high-performance method for evaluating Newtonian potentials in two-dimensional domains, specifically those with smooth boundaries. Our approach utilizes a type of quadrature known as the Clenshaw-Curtis formula, which is particularly effective when the domain is a square or can be easily transformed into one. By applying the transformation technique, we can adapt our method to compute Newtonian potentials for irregular planar domains. Our algorithm employs a recursive set of functions that can be evaluated efficiently using a recursive Clenshaw-Curtis formula, which in turn enables fast computation of the Newtonian potential. We can compute this using roughly proportional steps to the number of grid cells in the domain, making our method suitable for large-scale simulations. We compare our new method to established techniques, particularly showing its performance gains with respect to speed and memory usage in various scenarios. Furthermore, we offer our implementation as an open-source library for use with the Python programming language. The source code can be found at: https://github.com/numericalcuba/PyNBI/. The new method can also be accessed as part of the PDE/BESOLV solvers in the Cuba library, which is available at: https://github.com/numericalcuba/Cuba/. Additionally, we provide a brief overview of how the new method can be combined with the Newton iteration technique to solve Poisson's equation for multiple function inputs. This hybrid approach can solve such equations faster and with greater efficiency, particularly in scenarios involving large datasets. The new method can also be used to compute Green's functions and other related potentials. The new method has already been used to model the behavior of dust in galaxy clusters, as demonstrated in the accompanying poster presentation, and is now available for use in the GHOST code, a high-performance, open-source astrophysics simulation library.
